title: The Floor That Keeps Moving
question: How does new ocean floor form, and where does it go?
hook: The rock of the ocean floor is youngest at its central ridges and gets older the farther you travel from them.
idea: At mid-ocean ridges, rising magma builds new crust that moves away on both sides, so oceans widen and their rocks age with distance from the ridge.

beats.prompt: A magnetometer is towed across a mid-ocean ridge from one side to the other. What pattern of magnetic stripes will it record?

choices.label: Random stripes with no pattern
choices.feedback: Tempting if reversals seem chaotic, but the stripes are far from random: each side repeats the other.

choices.label: Stripes on one side mirror the other
One uniform field with no stripes
choices.feedback: It would hold if the field never flipped, but the record shows past reversals as distinct stripes.

choices.label: Stripes only on the older side
choices.feedback: Both sides are made of crust from the same ridge, so both carry stripes.

beats.explain: New crust forms at the ridge and moves off to both sides, so the stripes on one side are the mirror image of those on the other.

beats.prompt: Put these steps from a continental rift to a new sea in order.
items: Heating at the base of the continental crust
The heated area rises into a broad dome
Fractures in the bowed crust grow into rifts
A rift opens into the ocean and floods as a new sea
beats.explain: Heat makes the crust less dense so it domes up, the bowing crust cracks into rifts, and when a rift reaches the existing ocean, seawater floods in.

beats.prompt: Sort each ridge spreading rate into its group.
items: Over 200 mm/yr, East Pacific Rise in the Miocene
beats.explain: Fast ridges open at more than 90 mm a year and slow ridges at less than 40 mm a year.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong; which?
steps: Basaltic magma rises at a spreading center and cools into new seabed
The new seabed then moves away from the ridge
So the oldest rock on the plate sits right at the ridge crest
Spreading like this helps explain how continents drift
beats.explain: Because new rock keeps forming at the ridge and moving outward, the youngest rock is near the spreading zone and older rock lies farther away.
